title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
gist: Binance suffered an apparent record $6.3 billion hack, linked by TRM Labs to North Korea's TraderTraitor, via a compromised engineer laptop. Binance says it has reserved over $6.34 billion to cover losses and expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours. Stablecoin issuers froze funds.

insights.claim: Binance put the estimated total impact of the hack at about $6.3 billion, which analysts call almost certainly the largest theft of any kind in history.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Record loss at the largest exchange is a systemic confidence shock for crypto.
insights.quote: This is almost certainly the largest theft of any kind in history

insights.claim: An initial investigation found hackers compromised an engineer's laptop, and further investigation uncovered additional points of breach; Binance found no evidence private keys were breached.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Operational security at exchanges, not cryptography, is the weak link.

insights.claim: TRM Labs linked the hack to North Korean unit TraderTraitor, following the $1.5 billion Bybit theft last year; Chainalysis says North Korea stole about $2 billion in 2025, up 50 percent.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: State-sponsored theft is escalating and funds sanctioned regimes.

insights.claim: Elliptic says the attacker converted about $3.3 billion into assets that cannot be frozen, such as ETH, and is working to cash out, while $2.8 billion of frozen crypto was verified.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Stolen ETH selling could weigh on prices.

insights.claim: Binance says it reserved over $6.34 billion to cover the incident, with $5 billion already in the affected tokens, and is buying more tokens, which may take longer for illiquid ones.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Token buying to make users whole could add market demand but is constrained by liquidity.

insights.claim: CZ said the reserve fund holds about $1 billion in bitcoin, leaving roughly $2 billion to cover, and noted Binance owns SpaceX shares worth over $1 billion; annual revenue is about $5 billion.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Binance appears solvent on its own claims, but coverage depends on asset sales.
insights.locator: Zhao said this leaves roughly $2 billion

insights.claim: Binance expects to allow withdrawals again within 48 hours, and bitcoin fell about 4 percent before regaining to trade above $78,000.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Muted price reaction suggests the market sees the loss as contained.

insights.claim: Tether froze about $1.5 billion of USDT and Circle said $800 million of USDC was frozen.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Issuer freeze power shows stablecoin centralization as a control but also a censorship risk.
insights.locator: In a sign of the potential repercussions

insights.claim: Crypto exchanges hold big piles of customer assets, so some institutions use third-party custody; Binance works with Swiss banks Sygnum and Flow.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Off-exchange custody should gain demand after this heist.

insights.claim: Binance was ordered to wind down EU operations in July after failing to get a license, became regulated in Abu Dhabi in December 2025, and pleaded guilty in 2023 paying a $4.3 billion fine.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.locator: Binance was ordered to wind down

insights.claim: Crypto is in a prolonged downturn after a late-last-year sell-off wiped more than $1 trillion from market capitalization, and other 2026 hacks include Bitget (~$390 million) and Drift ($280 million).
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Weak market plus hack frequency raise counterparty risk.
insights.locator: The crypto market is in the grip
